newsitem.title: LIBERIA: No new date yet for Liberian elections.
newsitem.headline: No new date yet for Liberian elections.

text.p: Former Liberian warlords on Friday met Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha but failed to agree on a date to hold Liberia's general election originally scheduled for May 30, delegates said.

The talks will continue on Saturday in greater detail with Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi, the only woman presidential candidate among the Liberians, Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, told reporters after the four-hour meeting with Abacha.

"Perhaps on the basis of the analysis tomorrow appropriate recommendations would be made to the Nigerian head of state on which he would take a position and put it forward to the ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) meeting that will be held next week," she said.
Abacha told the gathering of about 100 Liberians there was a limit to how much sacrifice West African nations could make to maintain peace in Liberia.
The May date was part of a peace plan brokered in Abuja last August by ECOWAS, of which Abacha is chairman, and backed by the Nigerian-led African peacekeeping force ECOMOG.
Most of the Liberian leaders have called for a postponement for security reasons and lack of voter education.

"May 30 now looks impossible but we on our part are looking at the end of June," said an aide to former warlord Charles Taylor, who launched the Liberian civil war in 1989 and is a leading presidential candidate.
"There will be a consensus on a date but the delay should not be too long because Liberia needs a president as soon as possible to lead the nation," the Taylor aide told Reuters.
The talks were attended by the presidential candidate and chairman of each of the 16 political parties in Liberia, the West African country founded by freed American slaves in 1847.
Fifteen of the parties, except Taylor's National Patriotic Front of Liberia (NPFL), have asked for the polls to be delayed until August or September to ensure credible results.

Johnson-Sirleaf told reporters in Lagos this week that all parties except NPFL felt May 30 was not feasible. Abacha will next week host a meeting of the ECOWAS Committee of Nine on Liberia to decide finally whether to shift the polls.

Apart from killing more than 150,000 people, the Liberian civil war displaced half the pre-war population of 2.5 million. Hundreds of thousands of Liberians are refugees in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone. Others are in Ghana and Nigeria.
